extracted.intended_audience: state and local air agencies (SIP submitters), regulated sources in nonattainment areas, EPA reviewers, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and proposed approval of a State Implementation Plan (SIP) revision submitted as an equivalent alternative to a Clean Air Act (CAA) section 185 fee program for the revoked 1997 8-hour ozone NAAQS. The rubric covers enforceability, fee-equivalence demonstration, reporting, and procedural requirements for EPA approval and public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness criteria (40 CFR part 51, appendix V)
rubrics_metrics.description: On July 10, 2024, the submittal for SJVUAPCD Rule 3171 was deemed by operation of law to be complete. We have reviewed the submittal to ensure it meets the completeness criteria in 40 CFR part 51, appendix V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SIP submissions must meet the formal completeness requirements in 40 CFR part 51, appendix V before EPA proceeds with substantive review; EPA may rely on the date a submittal is deemed complete to trigger review timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIP rules must be enforceable
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules in the SIP must be enforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluates whether the submitted rule contains enforceable requirements (e.g., clear obligations, monitoring/recordkeeping, penalties or mechanisms to ensure compliance) consistent with federal SIP enforceability standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-interference with attainment and reasonable further progress (110(a)(2) and 110(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules in the SIP must not interfere with applicable requirements concerning attainment and reasonable further progress or other CAA requirements. See, respectively, CAA sections 110(a)(2) and 110(l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA assesses whether the submitted revision would relax, delay, or otherwise impede attainment of the NAAQS or reasonable further progress; the SIP revision must preserve current applicable attainment/RFP obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with CAA section 185 statutory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA is also evaluating this rule for consistency with the statutory requirements of CAA section 185.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a section 185-equivalent alternative, EPA evaluates whether the program meets the core statutory objectives and mechanisms of section 185 (i.e., fee assessment and use conditioned on nonattainment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative program must be consistent with section 172(e) and 'not less stringent' than statutory section 185
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the rule allows for an equivalent alternative program to meet the CAA section 185 obligation for the revoked 1997 8-hour ozone NAAQS, it must be consistent with the principles of CAA section 172(e) and must be 'not less stringent' than the statutory section 185 program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA looks for a demonstration that alternative measures are at least as protective/stringent as collecting statutory section 185 fees from major stationary sources; equivalency may be shown via revenue/benefit comparisons and program design consistent with 172(e) principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual payment of fees computed according to section 185(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under sections 182(d)(3), (e), (f) and 185 of the Act, states with ozone nonattainment areas classified as Severe or Extreme are required to submit a SIP revision that requires major stationary sources of VOC or NOX emissions in the area to pay a fee if the area fails to attain the standard by the attainment date. The required SIP revision must provide for annual payment of the fees, computed in accordance with section 185(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when an alternative program is used, the SIP must implement the same annual-fee concept and ensure fee amounts are computed in the manner required by section 185(b) or that the alternative demonstrates equivalent effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of the CAA section 185 fee obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule includes calculation of the CAA section 185 fee obligation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission should show how the section 185 fee would be calculated for each covered major stationary source, or provide an alternative calculation that is transparently comparable to the statutory calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a fee equivalency demonstration system and produce annual fee-equivalency reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule includes establishment of a CAA section 185 fee equivalency demonstration system, an annual fee equivalency demonstration report, reporting to the EPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SIP must create a mechanism and documentation to demonstrate each year that the alternative program's revenues and/or emission reductions meet or exceed what would have resulted from the statutory fee program; annual reports and EPA reporting are required to verify equivalency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision requiring major sources to pay fees in the event of a collection shortfall
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule includes a provision requiring major sources to pay fees directly in the event of a fee collection shortfall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The alternative program must include a backstop so that, if alternative funding sources fall short, the statutory-fee-equivalent amount is recovered from the originally-covered major stationary sources to ensure fee equivalence is achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include California Vehicle Code (DMV) fees as additional funding but demonstrate revenue equivalence (>= statutory revenue)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee equivalency demonstration system includes fees collected by the California Department of Motor Vehicles as an additional source of funding for the alternative 185 fee program and would need to demonstrate that the program's revenue would be greater than or equal to the revenue that would result under a direct implementation of the section 185 fee program if all major stationary sources covered by section 185 paid the statutory fee amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If non-stationary-source fees (e.g., DMV fees) are counted, the SIP must quantitatively compare combined revenues to the statutory-fee baseline and show revenues meet or exceed that baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of collected fees to establish and implement surplus incentive-based emissions-reduction programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees that are collected are used to establish and implement surplus incentive-based emissions-reduction programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluates whether fee expenditures are directed toward programs that produce enforceable, surplus, and quantifiable emission reductions consistent with the equivalency demonstration and CAA objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with EPA guidance documents (General Preamble, Bluebook, Little Bluebook)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and policy documents that we used to evaluate enforceability, revision/relaxation, and rule stringency requirements for the applicable criteria pollutants include: the General Preamble for Title I implementation (57 FR 13498; 57 FR 18070), the Bluebook (Issues Relating to VOC Regulation Cutpoints...), and the Little Bluebook (Guidance Document for Correcting Common VOC & Other Rule Deficiencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA applies principles and interpretations from established guidance when judging enforceability, cutpoints, deficiencies, deviations, rule relaxations, and stringency; submissions should address or be consistent with these documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference requirements (1 CFR 51.5) and availability of materials
rubrics_metrics.description: In this rule, the EPA is proposing to include in a final EPA rule regulatory text that includes incorporation by reference. In accordance with requirements of 1 CFR 51.5, the EPA is proposing to incorporate by reference SJVUAPCD Rule 3171... The EPA has made, and will continue to make, these materials available through https://www.regulations.gov and at the EPA Region IX Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When incorporating state rule text into the CFR, the SIP submission and EPA's final rule must comply with 1 CFR 51.5 (proper citation and availability); supporting materials must be accessible via the docket and at EPA offices for inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment submission requirements and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your comments, identified by Docket ID No. EPA-R09-OAR-2025-0300 at https://www.regulations.gov. For comments submitted at Regulations.gov, follow the online instructions for submitting comments. Once submitted, comments cannot be edited or removed from Regulations.gov. The EPA may publish any comment received to its public docket. Do not submit electronically any information you consider to be Confidential Business Information (CBI) or other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute. Multimedia submissions (audio, video, etc.) must be accompanied by a written comment. The written comment is considered the official comment and should include discussion of all points you wish to make. The EPA will generally not consider comments or comment contents located outside of the primary submission (i.e., on the web, cloud, or other file sharing system).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must follow docket identification and site-specific rules; submitters should avoid placing CBI in public dockets, ensure multimedia has an accompanying written document, and rely only on the primary submission method to ensure EPA will consider the comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of EPA approval: approve state choices that meet CAA and federal regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Clean Air Act, the Administrator is required to approve a SIP submission that complies with the provisions of the Act and applicable federal regulations. Thus, in reviewing SIP submissions, the EPA's role is to approve state choices, provided that they meet the criteria of the Clean Air Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA does not substitute its policy preferences for state law where the submission meets CAA requirements; approval is limited to checking statutory/regulatory compliance, not to imposing additional federal requirements beyond state law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional limitation: SIP not approved to apply on Indian reservation land or where Tribe has jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition, the SIP is not approved to apply on any Indian reservation land or in any other area where the EPA or an Indian Tribe has demonstrated that a Tribe has jurisdiction. In those areas of Indian country, the rule does not have Tribal implications and will not impose substantial direct costs on Tribal governments or preempt Tribal law as specified by Executive Order 13175.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must respect jurisdictional limits; EPA approvals apply only where state authority exists and do not extend to areas under tribal jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible program design features (partial exemptions and alternative baselines) only if equivalency ensured
rubrics_metrics.description: The equivalent alternative program provides a partial exemption for certain clean emissions units, and it allows for an alternative baseline in certain situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program features such as exemptions or alternative baselines may be permitted, but EPA will evaluate them for their effect on aggregate fee collection and emission reductions; any such features are acceptable only if the overall program remains 'not less stringent' and meets the fee-equivalency demonstration.
